confidence_notes: I made 3 web searches. The FX value is the RBA 4:00 pm AUD/USD reading of 0.6720 for 18 November 2026. I got it from a search summary that cites the RBA exchange rates page, but I did not open the RBA page directly. Restaurant and coffee anchors come from search summaries of cost-of-living aggregators (Numbeo, Wise, Expatistan, Livingcost, Hikersbay). For Buenos Aires city, the inexpensive meal was about USD 14-26, cappuccino about USD 3.5-5.6, mid-range dinner for two about USD 46-90, and draught beer about USD 3.6-5.5. I picked central values. The aggregators disagree by up to about 40% because of peso conversion differences and Argentina's currency volatility. Beer, cocktail and wine use 2026 peso bar menu prices reported by a La Nacion article and a Darsena Bar menu: draught beer about ARS 6,000-7,000, house cocktails about ARS 9,000-10,000, and happy-hour glasses of wine about ARS 4,500-5,100. I converted them at roughly ARS 1,450-1,530 per USD and adjusted upward from happy-hour prices. The cocktail and wine figures are less certain than the beer figure. Most data is from late 2026 rather than July 2026, and peso-dollar movements add uncertainty. Accommodation anchors are my own estimates from general knowledge for July, which is the southern-winter shoulder or low season. I did not search accommodation prices or check any listings, so these are the least certain anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink figures are based on searched aggregator data for Buenos Aires itself. Accommodation is benchmarked against other large Latin American capitals with strong tourism, such as Santiago and Mexico City. I also assumed Buenos Aires has become more expensive in USD since the peso strengthened in 2024-2026.
